drivingQuestion: If one scheduled work for the Festival and died, are his sons penalized?
outcomeNote: The dilemma continues and is answered in the next unit.

segments.he: וְשׁוֹלֶה פִּשְׁתָּנוֹ מִן הַמִּשְׁרָה כּוּ׳. בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא: כִּוֵּון מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּמּוֹעֵד וָמֵת, מַהוּ שֶׁיִּקְנְסוּ בָּנָיו אַחֲרָיו?
segments.en: The mishna states: «And he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool» so that it is not ruined from soaking too long in the water, provided that he does not plan from the outset to do his work on the intermediate days of the Festival. And with regard to anyone, if he planned from the outset to perform his labor on the intermediate days of the Festival, the fruit of that labor must be destroyed. «Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:» If «one planned» from the outset to perform «his labor on» the intermediate days of «a Festival, and he died» after doing so, «what is» the halakha? «Should his children be penalized after him» and have to lose the products of their father’s labor?
